card.name: Pediatric cancer treatment text
card.fires_on: Scattered words in pediatric oncology text, often a linking word like 'with', 'for' or 'of' just before a cancer name or abbreviation, or the middle of 'refractory'. It also fires on the first letter of drug or tumor names such as liraglutide or LGG.

modes.label: Linking word before a cancer
modes.description: A small word like with, of or for right after 'pediatric patients' or 'children', before a named cancer.
modes.example: Recommended Dosage Reductions for Adverse Reactions for Pediatric Patients<< with>> ALCL or IMT and Young Adults

modes.label: Start of a drug or tumor name
modes.description: A single letter or bracket starting a drug name or cancer abbreviation.

modes.label: Inside leukemia description
modes.description: Partway through 'refractory' in a description of relapsed leukemia in children.
modes.example: clofarabine in pediatric patients with relapsed or refr<<actory>> acute leukemia

card.writes: No clear meaning; it slightly favors name-like fragments and disfavors 'plasma' and 'multiple'.
card.plain: It lights up on small connecting words and name beginnings in text about cancer drugs and children with cancer.
